title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Permutation and Combination
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: The number of groups of three or more distinct numbers that can be chosen from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 so that the groups always include 3 and 5, while 7 and 8 are never included together is
questions.explain:
We need to form subsets of size $\ge 3$ from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} containing 3 and 5, but not both 7 and 8.
Since 3 and 5 are strictly included, the base group is {3, 5} (size 2). 
We must choose elements from the remaining 6 numbers: {1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8}.
Since the final group must have at least 3 numbers, we must pick at least 1 number from the remaining 6.
Total subsets of the 6 remaining numbers = $2^6 = 64$.
The empty set (choosing 0 numbers) leaves the group at {3, 5} (size 2, invalid). Thus, $64 - 1 = 63$ valid subsets if no other restriction.
Now we exclude subsets that contain BOTH 7 and 8.
If we fix 7 and 8 in the selection, we can freely choose from the other 4 numbers {1, 2, 4, 6}. There are $2^4 = 16$ such combinations.
All 16 of these have size $\ge 2$ (so they never intersect with the empty set).
Valid groups = Total subsets (64) - Empty set (1) - Sets containing both 7 & 8 (16) = $64 - 1 - 16 = 47$.
